builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
summary: Replaces exact GP log-marginal-likelihood training over full dense kernel matrices with a low-rank FITC objective and analytic gradients computed from low-rank factors and small dense matrices, all in single precision. Costs are the engineering of a custom training pipeline and an approximation rank that must be tuned per dataset, with fp16/TF32 variants adding complexity for only modest speedups. It can fail on ill-conditioned problems, where single precision limits the full-kernel predictive solve and reduced-precision variants become unreliable.
rationale: The method is implementable on a single 24 GB GPU and validated on real regression benchmarks, but the dataset-dependent rank and conditioning-sensitive precision limits require workload-specific validation before production adoption, and it applies only if the reader actually uses Gaussian processes.
technique: Low-rank single-precision Gaussian process training (AnchorNet + FITC)

claims.statement: Replaces exact GP log-marginal-likelihood training over full dense kernel matrices with a low-rank FITC objective and analytic gradients computed from low-rank factors and small dense matrices, all in single precision. Costs are the engineering of a custom training pipeline and an approximation rank that must be tuned per dataset, with fp16/TF32 variants adding complexity for only modest speedups. It can fail on ill-conditioned problems, where single precision limits the full-kernel predictive solve and reduced-precision variants become unreliable.

Reaches reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time across nine large-scale regression datasets; no speedup factor is stated, and required approximation rank varies per dataset.
